marketing.affiliate.processTitle: Three steps to your first commission
marketing.affiliate.step1: Sign up free on Creem and get your referral link right away. No approval needed.
marketing.affiliate.step2: Post the link in your videos, articles or community. Every subscription made through it is tracked to you.
marketing.affiliate.step3: Earn {percent}% of each subscriber's payments for their first {months} months, paid out by Creem.
marketing.affiliate.faqJoin.question: How do I join?
marketing.affiliate.faqJoin.answer: Sign up at {joinUrl}. There is no approval step, so you can start right away. Sign in with Google or a magic link (if this is your first Creem affiliate program, you'll also fill in a short profile), and your referral link, clicks, referred customers and commission earnings all appear in your dashboard.
marketing.affiliate.faqTracking.question: How are my referrals tracked?
marketing.affiliate.faqTracking.answer: When someone clicks your link, Creem records the click and sends them to anytranslator.app. If they buy a plan on our website in the same browser within {days} days of the click, the sale is credited to you, even if they look at other pages first or come back later. A purchase may not be credited if it is made on a different device or browser, in a private window, after cookies or site data were cleared, or with cookies blocked. Each purchase is credited to one affiliate only.
marketing.affiliate.faqAppStore.question: Do purchases made in the iPhone app count?
marketing.affiliate.faqAppStore.answer: No. Only plans bought on anytranslator.app through Creem's checkout earn commission. Subscriptions bought inside the iOS app through the App Store are handled by Apple, not Creem, so they earn no commission.
marketing.affiliate.faqCommission.question: How much do I earn?
marketing.affiliate.faqCommission.answer: You earn {percent}% of every payment from customers you refer, renewals included, on all web plans (Standard and Voice; weekly, monthly and yearly). Commissions stop {months} months after the first attributed sale. The percentage is calculated after Creem's 2% affiliate platform fee, so a $100 sale pays commission on $98.
marketing.affiliate.faqPlanChange.question: What if a customer changes plans, or cancels and subscribes again later?
marketing.affiliate.faqPlanChange.answer: Each payment Creem attributes to your link earns {percent}%, for up to {months} months from the first attributed sale. Creem has not published separate rules for plan changes or resubscribing, so check your dashboard for what was credited.
marketing.affiliate.faqRefund.question: What happens if a customer gets a refund?
marketing.affiliate.faqRefund.answer: New commissions stay pending for a 7–12 day hold, a risk check required by Creem's payment partners, before they move to your available balance. Refunds are issued through Creem, the seller of record, which also manages chargebacks. Creem does not publish how a refund or chargeback changes an affiliate's commission, so check each commission's status (pending, approved, paid) in your dashboard.
marketing.affiliate.faqPayout.question: How and when do I get paid?
marketing.affiliate.faqPayout.answer: Creem pays you directly. Before your first withdrawal, complete identity verification (KYC) and set up a payout method: bank transfer (via Paysway) or USDC on Polygon (via Mural). Each commission is held for 7-12 days before it becomes part of your available balance. Once your available balance reaches 50 USD or 50 EUR, click Withdraw on the Balance page; payouts are not automatic. Your payout is then processed in the next window on the 1st or 15th of the month (the next business day if that date falls on a weekend or public holiday).
marketing.affiliate.faqVerify.question: What do I need before my first payout?
marketing.affiliate.faqVerify.answer: You need two things, both set up on the Payouts page. First, identity verification through Sumsub with a government-issued ID and a selfie. This typically takes 1–2 working days. Second, a payout method: bank transfer (via Paysway) or USDC (via Mural). Once both are done, you can withdraw when your available balance reaches 50 USD.
marketing.affiliate.faqFees.question: Are there payout fees or tax documents?
marketing.affiliate.faqFees.answer: Bank transfers (via Paysway) cost 7 USD/EUR or 1% of the payout, whichever is higher; USDC on Polygon (via Mural) costs 2%. If your bank account's currency differs from your commission currency, the payment provider may add a conversion fee. After each payout you can download a reverse invoice from the Payout Activity tab for your tax records.
marketing.affiliate.faqSelfReferral.question: Can I use my own link?
marketing.affiliate.faqSelfReferral.answer: No. Buying through your own referral link, or through accounts you control, isn't allowed in this program and doesn't qualify for commission. Members of the AnyTranslator team can't be affiliates.
marketing.affiliate.faqPromote.question: How can I promote AnyTranslator, run paid ads, and use the name and logo?
marketing.affiliate.faqPromote.answer: Share your link anywhere you introduce the app honestly, such as reviews, videos, blogs, social posts and newsletters. Paid ads are allowed, as long as you don't bid on 'AnyTranslator' or similar brand keywords in search ads. Also, don't post your link on coupon or deal sites, send spam, or make claims about the app that aren't true. Partners who break these rules may be removed from the program and stop earning new commissions. You can use the AnyTranslator name, the unmodified logo and your own screenshots of the app to describe it accurately. Don't change the logo. Don't use the name or logo as your own brand or in your account names or domain names. Don't suggest that you are AnyTranslator or speak for it.
marketing.affiliate.faqReferredPrice.question: Does buying through a referral link cost more?
marketing.affiliate.faqReferredPrice.answer: No. The price is the same with or without a referral link, because the commission comes out of our share. Creem is the seller of record, so 'Creem' appears on your payment statement and Creem handles sales tax or VAT.
marketing.affiliate.faqReferredApp.question: I bought on the website. How do I use my plan in the app, and how do I cancel?
marketing.affiliate.faqReferredApp.answer: After checkout you get two emails. One is from AnyTranslator, with a link that activates your plan in the AnyTranslator app. The other is your payment receipt from Creem, our payment provider, with a link to the Creem Customer Portal. To cancel, open the Customer Portal from that receipt link and cancel your subscription there.
marketing.faq.FreeQ: Can I try it for free?
marketing.faq.FreeA: Try translation, the AI assistant, voice and basic Widget content for free; check the App for allowances. PRO adds multi-page scans, more Helper settings and custom learning content. Voice plans include more minutes.
marketing.faq.AgentQ: How is AI assistant voice different from voice translation?
marketing.faq.AgentA: For face-to-face chats, use voice translation for bilingual subtitles and natural AI speech. For questions or speaking practice, talk to the AI assistant and follow its examples. They use separate minute allowances.
marketing.voice.title: Understand it. Say it naturally.

marketing.faq.ScanQ: Should I choose Menu, Document or Table?
marketing.faq.ScanA: Menu lets you choose dishes and extras, then show an order in the original language. Document organises paragraphs by page; Table keeps rows and columns. Scan 1 photo at a time for free, or up to 10 per batch with PRO. Reopen results from scan history.
marketing.faq.AccuracyQ: How can I check Russian and German cases and endings?
marketing.faq.AccuracyA: Use Helper's Grammar, Common mistakes and Word-by-word analysis to understand Russian and German cases and endings. To revise your source sentence, ask the AI assistant to proofread it and explain why.

Use voice translation to ask staff about portions, ingredients and preparation.
Rehearse follow-up questions with the AI assistant; confirm allergies directly with staff.
messages: Change language and tone in the original text field, without switching Apps.
Compare a long message with its source in text translation, hear pronunciation and save useful phrases.
Give the AI assistant the background to find a reply that fits the situation.
reading: Choose Document for notices, leaflets and multi-page papers; read paragraphs, lists and tables by page.
Choose Table for timetables and price lists; scroll across rows and columns and compare the source and units.
Bring difficult sentences into text translation and let Helper explain their usage.
study: Practise scenes and set goals with the AI assistant before your next real conversation.
Use Helper to understand grammar, vocabulary and examples wherever you get stuck.
Listen and review useful phrases with the learning Widget, turning spare moments into practice.
media: Follow videos with subtitles or read webpages with screen text, keeping content and translation together.
Copy phrases into the AI assistant to ask about meaning, compare wording and practise.
Choose a suitable tone in text translation, then use what you've understood in your next reply.

articles.voice.intro: Use bilingual subtitles and natural AI speech for in-person conversations. Choose AI assistant voice for examples and practice. For other Apps' videos, use Video subtitles in Cross-App translation.
articles.voice.tip: Choose both languages and an audio mode before you start. Replay AI speech and follow its tone and rhythm; revisit the conversation and summary to keep useful expressions.
articles.voice.limit: Two-way conversation suits face-to-face chats. Private listening uses an earpiece or headphones; Subtitles only suits quiet settings. Start video subtitles from Cross-App translation; capturable content depends on iOS.
articles.menu.intro: In Photos, choose Organise, then Menu. Add clear, straight-on photos of the full menu to organise names, ingredients, portions and prices into dishes.
articles.menu.tip: Read the dishes and prices, choose quantities, sizes or available extras, and add notes. Open the original-language order to show items, options and quantities to staff.
articles.menu.limit: Known prices are totalled separately by currency; no definite total is given for unclear prices. Confirm ingredients, allergens and preparation directly with staff before showing your order.
articles.work.intro: Translate Russian or German to understand it, then choose a tone for your reply. Helper explains cases and endings; explicitly ask the AI assistant if you want your original sentence proofread.
articles.work.tip: Match the tone to your reader: Polite for work requests, Letter for email and Friendly for familiar chats. Ask Helper about difficult sentences, then give the AI assistant context to compare replies.
articles.work.limit: Automatic tone preserves a whole passage already in the target language. For changes to cases, endings or grammar, use Helper to understand why, then explicitly ask the AI assistant to proofread.
articles.mac.intro: Translate text and ask AI questions on your Mac too. Check the App Store to see whether your model and system are supported.
articles.mac.tip: Once downloaded, translate text or use the AI assistant. Choose an image file or paste an image in Photos. Check your device's store page for compatibility and system requirements.
articles.mac.limit: The translation keyboard, Widget and Cross-App translation are primarily for supported iPhones/iPads. Available features depend on the actual App on each platform.
articles.keyboard.intro: Follow the App's guide to add the keyboard in iOS and enable Full Access for online translation. Type or use system dictation in supported fields, then translate and adjust the tone.
articles.keyboard.tip: Type or use native iOS dictation to draft, then choose a language and tone. Tools can also translate clipboard text, copy the result or insert it at the cursor.
articles.keyboard.limit: Keyboard and dictation availability depend on the App, iOS and language. Type instead or return to the main App when needed; download input language packs as guided.
articles.chat.intro: Treat the AI assistant as your pocket language coach: understand photos, interpret live or rehearse for travel and work. Start with a question and take that preparation into daily life.
articles.chat.tip: Start with a scene or goal, such as ordering or an interview, or create your own. Ask AI to slow down, follow its tone and rhythm, then talk, review feedback and save phrases to practise again.
articles.chat.limit: Internet and allowance required; voice needs microphone permission. Availability varies by version, language and service status. Verify important information. A custom goal replaces your current plan and progress. Check the App for remaining allowance.
articles.learning.intro: Practise the conversations you'll actually have. Choose goals and scenes with the AI assistant, then use feedback and review to make the phrases your own.
articles.learning.tip: Focus on one setting at a time: answer first, then compare natural wording. Ask AI to model tone and rhythm, use Helper to understand usage, and repeat with the learning Widget.
articles.learning.limit: AI practice requires internet and allowance. The learning Widget requires iOS 17 or later; custom content and settings vary by plan.
articles.screen.intro: Keep translation in view while watching videos or reading webpages. Use subtitles for audio and screen text for visible content, then compare in Picture in Picture and revisit important lines later.
articles.screen.tip: Choose subtitles for videos and screen text for webpages. Move Picture in Picture or scroll the original page to read the next passage. Stop the screen broadcast when done; reopen useful lines from history.
articles.screen.limit: Requires iOS/iPadOS 16 or later, Picture in Picture and internet. Protected content may not be translatable. Subtitles use voice minutes; screen text uses translation credits. Check your balance in the App.

manifesto.seoDescription: Different languages shouldn't mean a smaller life. AnyTranslator brings together the tools to understand, express yourself and practise—for life abroad, study and learning.
manifesto.title:
A different language.
Not a smaller life.
manifesto.lead: Far from home, you deserve the confidence to live freely.
manifesto.opening:
You go abroad to see more of the world and open more possibilities.
Language shouldn't make you live more cautiously once you get there.

chapters.title: Far from home. Still yourself.
paragraphs: You circle the supermarket and still buy the wrong thing. Someone at the counter says a lot; you catch a few words but hesitate to ask again. In class, you have a question, yet keep it to yourself.
A form, a school notice or a rental document can make an ordinary day feel harder than it should. You want to get things right, but even asking takes courage.
You have ideas. You're making the effort. Sometimes language simply leaves the real you outside the conversation.

chapters.title: Life doesn't ask every question the same way.
paragraphs: It might be an unfamiliar menu, a voice message from your landlord, an explanation at a service desk or a document you need to read carefully.
So help can't come in just one form. You shouldn't have to jump between several tools to eat a meal, send a reply or get something done.
AnyTranslator puts the tools you need within reach. One less moment of getting stuck means a little more confidence to live your day.

chapters.title: From understanding a sentence to taking the next step.
paragraphs: Photograph a label to know what you're buying. Read dishes and extras to order what you want. Organise notices and documents by page, with paragraphs, tables and key details you can check.
Let bilingual subtitles and natural AI speech help you communicate face to face. Choose a formal, friendly or concise tone for messages, then say what you mean in full.
Not ready to speak yet? Rehearse with the AI assistant. From travel and classes to interviews, practise what you want to say. Understanding, expression and learning belong in the same everyday life.

chapters.title: Every language deserves to be understood well.
paragraphs: Language means more than replacing words. The challenge might be Russian or German endings—or a phrase that only makes sense in the way people live locally.

We'll keep refining context, tone and explanations, with less widely spoken languages in mind too. Fewer speakers shouldn't mean less care. You deserve more than a translation: you deserve to understand why it works.
